results.title: Factorization of a group into subsets of given sizes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $k$ a natural number and $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ natural numbers. The group $G$ has a subset factorization of type $(a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$ when there are finite subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ such that $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$, that is, every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{k-1}$ with $x_i \in A_i$ for every $i$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.35: counterexamples to subset factorization of every length
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Finite groups without subset factorizations exist for every length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$ there are a finite group $G$ and natural numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$, each at least $2$, with $a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{k-1} = |G|$, such that there are no subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ and $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$, that is, with every element of $G$ a product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{k-1}$ where $x_i \in A_i$ for every $i$.

results.summary: Let $B_m(x)$ denote the $m$-th Bernoulli polynomial. For $n \ge 0$, the Euler polynomial $E_n(x)$ is the polynomial with rational coefficients $E_n(x) = \frac{2}{n + 1} \left(B_{n+1}(x) - 2^{n+1} B_{n+1}(x/2)\right)$.

results.title: Fuel-bounded recurrence for the Euler numbers of order α
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E_m(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial. For a complex number $\alpha$, the complex numbers $a_\alpha(f, n)$, for natural numbers $f$ (the fuel) and $n$, are defined by $a_\alpha(0, n) = 1$, $a_\alpha(f + 1, 0) = 1$ and $a_\alpha(f + 1, n + 1) = -\alpha \, a_\alpha(f, n) + \frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_\alpha(f, k) \, E_{n-k}(0)$.

results.title: Euler numbers of order α
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E_m(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial. For a complex number $\alpha$, the Euler numbers of order $\alpha$ are the complex numbers $E_n^{(\alpha)}(0)$, $n \ge 0$, defined by $E_0^{(\alpha)}(0) = 1$ and $E_{n+1}^{(\alpha)}(0) = -\alpha E_n^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} E_k^{(\alpha)}(0) \, E_{n-k}(0)$ for $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Euler polynomials of order α
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a complex number $\alpha$ and $n \ge 0$, let $E_k^{(\alpha)}(0)$ denote the Euler numbers of order $\alpha$. The Euler polynomial of order $\alpha$ is the complex polynomial $E_n^{(\alpha)}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} E_k^{(\alpha)}(0) \, x^{n-k}$.

results.title: Euler polynomials at (x + 1)/2 via generalized Stirling polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_n(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial, $\alpha_k$ the Taylor coefficients of $(2 + 2z)/(2 + 2z + z^2)$, and $S(n, k, x) = \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{k}{j} (-1)^{k-j} (x + j)^n$ the generalized Stirling polynomial. For every $n \ge 0$, as polynomials in $x$ with rational coefficients, $2^n E_n\left(\frac{x + 1}{2}\right) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} k! \, \alpha_k \, S(n, k, x)$.

results.title: Recurrence for Euler polynomials of order α
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_m(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial and $E_m^{(\alpha)}(x)$ the Euler polynomial of order $\alpha$. For every complex number $\alpha$ and every integer $n \ge 1$, as polynomials in $x$, $E_n^{(\alpha)}(x) = (x - \alpha/2) \, E_{n-1}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n-2} \binom{n-1}{k} (-1)^{n-k} E_{n-1-k}(0) \, E_k^{(\alpha)}(x)$, where the sum is empty when $n = 1$.

results.title: Euler polynomials as alternating sums of shifted powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_n(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial. For all natural numbers $m \ge 2$ and $n \le 2m + 1$, $E_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{m} \frac{(-1)^k}{2^k} \binom{m+1}{k+1} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{k}{j} \left(x + j - \frac{k+1}{2}\right)^n$ as polynomials in $x$ with rational coefficients.

results.title: Euler polynomials via generalized Stirling polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_n(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial, $\alpha_k$ the Taylor coefficients of $(2 + 2z)/(2 + 2z + z^2)$, and $S(n, k, x) = \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{k}{j} (-1)^{k-j} (x + j)^n$ the generalized Stirling polynomial. For every integer $n \ge 1$, as polynomials in $x$ with rational coefficients, $2^n E_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} k! \, \alpha_k \, S(n, k, 2x - 1)$.

results.title: Double-sum formula for Euler polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_n(x)$ denote the Euler polynomial and $S(n, k, x) = \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{k}{j} (-1)^{k-j} (x + j)^n$ the generalized Stirling polynomial. For every $n \ge 0$, as polynomials in $x$ with rational coefficients, $2^n E_n(x) = \sum_{\ell=0}^{n} \frac{(-1)^\ell}{\ell + 1} \sum_{k=0}^{n-\ell} \frac{(k + \ell + 1)!}{2^k} \binom{\ell + 1}{k} S(n, k + \ell, 2x - 1)$.

results.title: Place
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. A place of $F/K$ is a valuation ring of $F$ containing $K$ and different from $F$: a $K$-subalgebra $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$ with $\mathcal{O} \neq F$ such that $z \in \mathcal{O}$ or $z^{-1} \in \mathcal{O}$ for every $z \in F$. results.title: Finitely many poles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. For every $x \in F$, there are only finitely many places $P$ of $F/K$ whose valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_P$ does not contain $x$, that is, $x$ has only finitely many poles. See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.3.4].

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $F$ a function field over $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. results.title: Clamped extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, its clamped extension is the function $\tilde f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $\tilde f(t) = f(\max(0, \min(1, t)))$. results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines and let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$. results.title: Labels of the composite machine
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines with label sets $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$, and let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$. The label set of their composite machine is the disjoint union of $\Lambda_1$, $\Lambda_2$ and two copies of $X \sqcup \{\bot\}$, one for each copy loop: in each copy, $\bot$ labels the step that pops and $x \in X$ labels the step that pushes $x$.

results.title: Hierarchy on a finite set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A hierarchy on a finite set `S`: a family of nonempty subsets of `S` containing `S` and every singleton, any two members nested or disjoint. These are the cluster systems of the rooted phylogenetic trees on `S` (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.5).

results.title: A binary hierarchy is a hierarchy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A binary hierarchy is a hierarchy.

results.title: Pairwise nested-or-disjoint clusters form a hierarchy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding `S` and the singletons to a family of pairwise nested-or-disjoint nonempty subsets of a nonempty `S` gives a hierarchy.

results.title: Hierarchies are refined by binary trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every family of pairwise nested-or-disjoint nonempty subsets of a nonempty `S` is contained in a binary hierarchy on `S`, the cluster set of a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on `S` (Semple & Steel 2003, Proposition 3.5.2 and the refinement of a rooted tree to a binary one).

results.title: Compatible splits
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The splits `A | Aᶜ` and `B | Bᶜ` are compatible: one of `A ∩ B`, `A ∩ Bᶜ`, `Aᶜ ∩ B`, `Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ` is empty (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.1).

results.summary: Compatibility depends only on the split, not on the side used to store it.

results.title: Split of a binary character
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Theorem

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: An unrooted binary tree is determined by its quartets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An unrooted binary tree is determined by its quartets (Semple & Steel 2003, Corollary 6.3.8): two trees displaying the same quartets are isomorphic. Already the quartets containing the taxon `a` suffice; they are the rooted triplets seen from `a`.
